references.text: Heaven and earth are mentioned as God's creation, the same elements that are called witnesses in Deuteronomy.
Moses calls heaven and earth to witness against Israel, using the same formula as in 30:19.
Blessing and curse are presented as choices for the people, reflecting the same theme of choosing between two ways.
The blessings that follow obedience to God's commands, linked to the choice between life and blessing.
The curses that follow disobedience, linked to the choice between death and curse.
Joshua challenges the people to choose whom they will serve, reflecting the same theme of making a choice.
Two ways are presented: the way of wisdom leading to life, and folly leading to death.
Heaven and earth are called as witnesses against Israel, serving the same witness function as in Deuteronomy.
God sets before the people the way of life and the way of death, a direct parallel to the choice between life and death.
God calls for repentance and life; he takes no pleasure in anyone's death, echoing the same appeal to choose life.
